tasks.title: Go for a one-hour walk together. Fresh air sparks good conversations.
tasks.detail: Movement and environment help get thoughts flowing. Let the conversation arise naturally. It's not about work, it's about getting to know each other. Use the time to understand how each person ticks.

tasks.title: Create mind maps about yourselves — origins, interests, values.
tasks.detail: Visualize what shapes and drives you. See commonalities and differences at a glance. Briefly present your mind maps and ask curious questions.

tasks.title: Find as many things you have in common as you can.
tasks.detail: Discover what connects you, from favorite foods to shared values. The more overlaps you find, the easier trust grows. Make sure everyone gets a chance to speak.

tasks.title: Team Charter: Why does our team exist? What goal are we pursuing?
tasks.detail: Define your mission and purpose together. A clear 'why' creates direction and motivation. Write the result somewhere visible as a foundation for later decisions.

tasks.title: Play a party game together — Taboo, Pictionary, Codenames, or Cards against Humanity.
tasks.detail: A shared game brings lightness and humor to the team. Make sure everyone can participate and no one feels exposed. Enjoy the time together.

tasks.title: Tell two truths and a lie about yourself. Guess each other's lies.
tasks.detail: A playful exercise to get to know each other better. Watch for surprises and laugh together at unexpected stories. Great for lightening the mood after a long workday.

tasks.title: Answer a few of the Dropbox questions that interest you.
tasks.detail: Pick 3–5 questions that spark curiosity — about childhood, learning, or values. The answers foster mutual understanding. Focus on truly listening, not commenting.

tasks.title: Retrospective: How does our collaboration feel so far?
tasks.detail: Pause and speak openly about how you work together. What's going well, where are the sticking points? Each person names one thing to keep or change.

tasks.title: Go out for lunch together — away from the office.
tasks.detail: A change of scenery opens up new conversations. Avoid work topics. Talk about experiences, interests, or plans instead. This strengthens connection beyond the professional realm.

tasks.title: Share the strengths you see in your teammates.
tasks.detail: Make appreciation visible. Everyone receives honest feedback about their strengths. Be specific and authentic. This builds trust and motivation.

tasks.title: Give yourselves a team name you all identify with. Not the lowest common denominator.
tasks.detail: A team name strengthens identity. Choose something that connects or inspires you — humor is welcome. The key is that everyone can see themselves in it.

tasks.title: Team Charter: How do we make decisions?
tasks.detail: Clarify how you reach decisions: by consensus, majority, or individual responsibility. Record who is involved when. This reduces misunderstandings in daily work.

tasks.title: Play a cooperative game together — Magic Maze, Order Overload, or Pandemic.
tasks.detail: Cooperative games foster joint planning and trust. Notice how you communicate and who takes the lead. Briefly discuss what stood out about your teamwork afterward.

tasks.title: Exercise in groups of three: Speak, Listen, Mirror.
tasks.detail: One person tells a story, the second listens actively, the third mirrors back what was heard. Then rotate. Focus on real listening, not giving advice. This strengthens empathy and presence.

tasks.title: Write short, personal thank-you notes to each team member over the next week.
tasks.detail: A handwritten thank-you has more impact than any email. Be specific about what you're grateful for. Notes can be anonymous or open. The key is sincerity.

tasks.title: Retrospective: What strengthens our trust?
tasks.detail: Collect moments where trust became visible. Talk about what makes you feel safe and what weakens trust. Derive small, concrete agreements from this.

tasks.title: Write down your teammates' quirks and edges, then play Bingo with them.
tasks.detail: A playful way to make individual traits visible. Keep it humorous, not hurtful. Afterwards discuss: which differences help us, which challenge us?

tasks.title: Create a team glossary with the 30 most important terms for your team.
tasks.detail: Collect jargon, abbreviations, and inside words. This builds shared understanding and helps new colleagues get up to speed faster.

tasks.title: Visualize: How do tasks actually flow around here?
tasks.detail: Map the typical journey from idea to outcome together. This makes bottlenecks and misunderstandings visible. Discuss where you can simplify or clarify.

tasks.title: Team Charter: What working practices do we want to keep or change?
tasks.detail: Reflect on your approach. What works well, what should change? Formulate 2–3 principles that matter to you. Display them visibly so they influence daily work.

tasks.title: Play a competitive game together — Settlers of Catan, 7 Wonders, or Risk.
tasks.detail: A bit of competition reveals how you handle pressure and ambition. Observe your reactions when it gets tight. Afterwards, talk openly about team dynamics and emotions.

tasks.title: Each person formulates a wish for the future: 'Something I wish from you…'
tasks.detail: Wishes are gentler than criticism and open up conversations. Be appreciative and clear. Note the wishes down to check later whether they had an effect.

tasks.title: Collect your achievements from recent months and celebrate them briefly.
tasks.detail: Bring back the pride! List what you've accomplished, big and small. A moment of recognition boosts motivation and cohesion.

tasks.title: Retrospective: Are we on track with our goal?
tasks.detail: Check your shared goal and progress toward it. Discuss what propels you and what holds you back. Conclude with a concrete decision on how to proceed.

tasks.title: Take a team photo you'd love to look at in retirement.
tasks.detail: A photo with meaning and a wink. Choose the motif, location, and mood together. It can be fun. The main thing is that it reflects your team feeling.

tasks.title: Us in 5 sentences: jointly formulate your self-image in five core statements.
tasks.detail: A condensed description of your identity. Discuss what makes you special, what you contribute, what you stand for. The sentences serve as guiding stars for future decisions.

tasks.title: Create an information radiator. Visualize your key metrics, learnings, and progress.
tasks.detail: A transparent overview of the team's status. Use a whiteboard or digital tool. Regular updates create focus and accountability.

tasks.title: Team Charter: What do we want to stand for?
tasks.detail: Condense your self-understanding into clear statements. What values and attitudes define you? This discussion strengthens your cultural clarity.

tasks.title: Plan a joint training — on communication or conflict resolution, for example.
tasks.detail: Learning together strengthens bonds. Choose a topic that truly affects you, and ensure shared reflection afterward. The key is that everyone takes something away.

tasks.title: Reflect on how you react in stressful situations.
tasks.detail: Collect typical stress moments and talk about your reactions. Understanding different patterns prevents escalation. Develop small aids for acute phases.

tasks.title: Share who shaped your conflict behavior — family, friends, or school.
tasks.detail: Biographical conversations build understanding for differences. Prioritize trust and voluntariness. You'll learn to take conflicts less personally.

tasks.title: Retrospective: What do we need to use conflicts productively?
tasks.detail: Discuss what conditions foster constructive disagreement. Connect these insights to your charter. This turns conflicts into learning moments rather than threats.

tasks.title: Hold a joke competition: the best joke wins.
tasks.detail: Humor relaxes and connects. Choose a format where everyone gets a turn. Keep it respectful and laugh together, not at each other.

tasks.title: Discuss how the Belbin role descriptions fit your team.
tasks.detail: Analyze your team roles: who brings which strengths and tasks? The discussion fosters understanding and balance. Use the insights to design responsibilities more consciously.

tasks.title: Try out different decision-making formats.
tasks.detail: Experiment with consent, majority vote, or delegation. Observe which method works when. This builds flexibility and clarity in decision-making.

tasks.title: Team Charter: Who does what and who is responsible for what?
tasks.detail: Document responsibilities and decision-making scopes. Clear roles prevent friction. Review regularly whether the allocation still fits.

tasks.title: Plan a joint volunteering activity — picking up trash or reforestation.
tasks.detail: Shared engagement creates meaning beyond work. Choose something that moves you and organize it yourselves. This strengthens cohesion and pride.

tasks.title: Discuss what types of conflict exist — misunderstanding, goal conflict, values conflict.
tasks.detail: Categorizing helps understand rather than avoid conflicts. Use examples from your practice. The goal is not to resolve them but to grasp them.

tasks.title: Discuss which values are touched in conflicts — fairness, pace, reliability.
tasks.detail: Values explain emotions. When you recognize which values are affected, you can discuss more respectfully. Make your most important values visible.

tasks.title: Retrospective: How do we treat each other when things get difficult?
tasks.detail: Treat difficult situations as learning opportunities. Collect what helped you — and what you want to do differently next time. Small agreements can have big impact.

tasks.title: Plan the celebration for reaching Level 12 together.
tasks.detail: Celebration strengthens community and motivation. Distribute tasks so everyone contributes. A good celebration honors the shared journey.

tasks.title: Each person names something they especially value about the others.
tasks.detail: Appreciation connects. Take time to be honest and specific. The moment stays in memory — often stronger than any feedback conversation.

tasks.title: Revise your team glossary and information radiator.
tasks.detail: Bring your documents up to date. What has changed, what has proven itself? Maintaining together shows responsibility and transparency.

tasks.title: Team Charter: What stays, what may change?
tasks.detail: Look back to the future: what do you want to preserve, what to let go of? This exercise ensures that development remains conscious.

tasks.title: Each person draws someone to give a symbolic gift at the closing celebration.
tasks.detail: A symbol or small gesture shows appreciation. Make sure the gifts are personal and respectful. This creates a connecting closing moment.

tasks.title: Visualize your journey — highlights, turning points, aha moments.
tasks.detail: Look back together and draw your path. This reflection strengthens pride and belonging. Use the insights for your next chapter.

tasks.title: Share what development you've seen in yourself and the team since Level 1.
tasks.detail: Reflection on change fosters awareness and maturity. Everyone shares what has grown — professionally and personally. Gratitude is welcome.

tasks.title: Celebrate reaching Level 12 — music, food, reflection, photos.
tasks.detail: A worthy conclusion to your shared journey. Enjoy the moment, share memories, and laugh together. This experience carries you into future challenges.
